identityReview: Ranil Wickremesinghe, born 24 March 1949, Sri Lankan UNP politician with an LLB and legal professional qualifications. Six premiership appointments are not continuous rule. First MP election 1977, parliamentary gap 2020–2021; old MP/president headings do not establish present office. Parliamentary election 20 July 2022 and presidential oath/assumption 21 July are separate. Successor’s term began 22 September 2024, with oath and transition on 23 September. Criminal investigation and procedural adjournment are not conviction.
lifeStatusEvidence: Daily Mirror’s 11 November 2026 court report states that Wickremesinghe and Saman Ekanayake were before the court when proceedings were adjourned. This is reported actual activity, rather than merely the future 9 December hearing. The Morning independently reports the adjournment but its short article does not separately establish personal attendance. No original courtroom video was viewed.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read historical parliamentary and party biographies, parliamentary election account, original 2022 and 2024 gazettes, archived Norwegian ceasefire statement, 2018 reinstatement report, IMF and World Bank releases, and 2025 arrest/2026 court reporting. Read Commons crop and parent licence/source metadata; government image source and licence PDF unavailable.
corrections: Read parliamentary profile: birth 24 March 1949, LLB and legal professional qualifications. The legislative table begins with the 1977 assembly and ends with the 2021–2022 parliamentary period; its MP heading is historical. A stale narrative says continuous service from 1978 for 28 years and is not used as current evidence. The table confirms prime minister from 12 May 2022 and finance/economic-stabilisation portfolio from 25 May. Its 2021 membership start is 18 June, whereas the election news item describes 23 June; the profile uses the year only and does not conflate selection, gazetting and oath. Conflicting fine-grained historical portfolio dates are not silently resolved.

Read Parliament’s 20 July 2022 election account: 134 votes for Wickremesinghe, 82 for Alahapperuma and three for Dissanayake; 223 cast, four invalid, two abstentions. This elected him to complete the predecessor’s term, not a fresh direct mandate. It corroborates 1977 entry, first premiership 7 May 1993–19 August 1994, subsequent terms and 12 May 2022 return. Its claim of full foreign-minister office at age 28 conflicts with the party biography’s deputy post; the deputy designation is retained. The page calls itself unedited and refers readers to Hansard. Its acting-president chronology and some 2015 dates are treated cautiously and not used to override gazettes.

Read original Gazette No. 2289/39 of 21 July 2022: elected by Parliament on 20 July; assumed office on 21 July for the unexpired period following Gotabaya Rajapaksa’s 14 July resignation. Eighth executive president is a narrower count than ninth president overall; no conflicting ordinal is used in the profile. The direct proclamation takes precedence over later summaries that put the oath on 22 July. Earlier acting powers are distinct from this assumption of the elected presidency.

Read original Gazette No. 2403/03 of 23 September 2024: Dissanayake was declared elected on 22 September; his term commenced on 22 September under Article 31(4); he took the oath and assumed office on 23 September under the stated constitutional provisions. The timeline records the 23 September transition while explicitly preserving the 22 September term start. It does not assume Wickremesinghe won a fresh term or remained president until the November parliamentary election. The five-year successor term is a legal term, not proof of future completion.

Read the Norwegian foreign minister’s 22 February 2002 announcement archived in USIP’s Peace Agreements Digital Collection: signed government/LTTE document deposited with Norway, ceasefire effective 00:00 on 23 February. Agreement and announcement are distinct from entry into force. Its aim was to support negotiation, not certify permanent peace or all parties’ later compliance. No casualty total or unsupported personal achievement claim is added. The archived statement is the date evidence; the separate agreement text supplies the structure, not a guessed signature date.

Read Sky News report dated 16 December 2018: Wickremesinghe was sworn in for a fifth time after Sirisena had replaced him with Mahinda Rajapaksa in October; parliamentary confidence disputes and court proceedings formed the background. His claim that removal was unlawful remains attributed. No full 2018 court docket was examined and no personal criminal verdict is inferred. A separate Daily Mirror report corroborates the oath but contains conflicting court dates and an impossible prorogation sequence; those details are not adopted.

Read IMF approval account dated 20 March 2023: 48-month EFF arrangement, SDR 2.286 billion, about US$3 billion at approval; immediate access to SDR 254 million, about US$333 million. Approval, immediate access and full disbursement are different. Macroeconomic and debt stability, fiscal reforms, governance and protection of vulnerable groups are program objectives, not proof they were already achieved. The party page’s early-March/US$330 million shorthand is replaced by the IMF record. Forecast table entries are not treated as actual 2026 outcomes.

Read World Bank release with body date 6 October 2026, despite URL path 2 October. It reports recovery of aggregate output but lagging household income and labour-market outcomes. It spans administrations and is not a causal attribution to Wickremesinghe or evidence he remained in office. The 4.4% annual growth figure is a projection, not a completed-year result. CMS fields contain unrelated Bahamas and placeholder-like metadata; country and date are taken from the substantive Sri Lanka text. No unverified country-classification claim or cross-methodology poverty comparison is used.

Read AP report of the 22 August 2025 arrest for alleged public-funds misuse during a UK stopover. This records allegations and custody, not guilt. The profile does not infer conviction or continuing detention in 2026 from the 2025 report.

Read Bhagya Silva’s 11 November 2026 Daily Mirror article body, not reader comments or its AI-summary interface. It reports Wickremesinghe and former presidential secretary Saman Ekanayake before Colombo Fort Acting Magistrate Kinsley Hettiarachchi and adjournment to 9 December for the Attorney General’s advice. This supports reported recent activity and an unresolved procedural stage; the December hearing has not yet occurred at the cutoff. No charge-sheet, final judgment, judicial transcript or original video was inspected.

Read UNP historical biography: six occasions as prime minister; first appointment after Premadasa’s assassination and during Wijetunga’s presidency; 2001–2004 and later terms; 2020–2021 parliamentary interruption; early deputy foreign-minister, youth and education roles. The page has dated presidential wording and self-promotional achievements, so it is not used to claim current presidency or independently measured economic/educational success. Its overall presidential ordinal differs from the gazette’s executive-presidency count. Its IMF timing and amounts are superseded by the fund’s own record.

additionalConsulted.access: Read ceasefire text, including signature/deposit mechanism, Norwegian notification of entry into force and termination clause. It does not by itself specify the calendar date; the Norwegian announcement supplies that date.
Read 23 September 2024 presidential-media statement reposted by the foreign ministry, corroborating the successor’s actual oath. The gazette separately specifies term commencement on 22 September.
Read short report of 11 November 2026 confirming the case was postponed to 9 December. It does not independently describe his physical attendance.

Read relevant historical chronology paragraphs, not the entire substantive emergency-regulations judgment. Paragraph 23 dates acting-president assumption to 15 July 2022, versus the parliamentary summary’s 14 July shorthand. Paragraph 29 gives a 22 July elected-presidential oath, contrary to the direct 21 July gazette; that later chronology is not used to override the proclamation. No conclusion about all emergency-rights litigation is asserted.
Read 16 December 2018 reinstatement report. Internal 13/14 December court-date and prorogation-date inconsistencies are excluded; the main profile cites the corroborating Sky account.
Observed Commons source link; opening timed out. Original government source not independently verified.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified human or native-language review. No original law degree certificate, exhaustive parliamentary date reconciliation, full 2018 court docket, complete later emergency-regulations judgment, original 2026 court transcript or charge-sheet, IMF disbursement ledger, causal economic impact audit, portrait pixels or independently retrieved GODL document. Macroeconomic recovery is not credited solely to one administration, and scheduled proceedings remain future events.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages checked for 24 March 1949 birth and LLB/advocate status; 1977 parliamentary entry and deputy rather than full foreign minister; 7 May 1993–19 August 1994 first premiership; 22 February 2002 announcement versus 23 February midnight ceasefire; 16 December 2018 reinstatement; 2020–2021 parliamentary gap; 12 May 2022 sixth premiership/25 May finance portfolio; 20 July parliamentary vote versus 21 July presidential assumption for an unexpired term; 20 March 2023 SDR 2.286 billion/approximately US$3 billion facility versus US$333 million immediate access; successor’s 22 September 2024 term start/23 September oath; attributed 6 October 2026 recovery assessment; August 2025 arrest allegations and actual 11 November 2026 court report versus future 9 December hearing.
